newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban say have taken northwest province.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban say have taken northwest province.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic movement said on Friday it had opened a new front against its rivals in the northwest and captured Badghis province.

A Taleban spokesman, quoted by a Pakistan-based Afghan news service, said the movement had attacked the forces of Uzbek chief Abdul Rashid Dostum to retaliate against his support for ousted government fighters in battles north of the capital Kabul.

The Afghan Islamic Press quoted Mullah Yar Mohammad, the Taleban governor of the western province of Herat, as saying Taleban forces took complete control of Badghis following heavy fighting against Dostum's troops since Thursday night.

Later, the Taleban forces advanced into the adjoining Dostum-held Faryab province and captured the southwestern district of Qaysar on Friday evening, he said. Dostum planes bombarded hilltops of the distict.

Dostum heads a newly formed alliance with the ousted government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani that fled from Kabul late last month and is pressing a demilitarisation of the Taleban-held capital as a condition for agreeing to a Pakistan-brokered ceasefire.
